## 固定收益開篇主論

美國就業全面回升，推動公債殖利率於9月4日走高，也讓聯準會升息重新成為9月政策辯論的核心，但賣壓仍集中於較短天期。8月非農就業增加16.2萬人，高於彭博調查的所有預估；修正數據不僅抹去原先公布的7月就業萎縮，6月與7月合計還上修5.5萬人。失業率維持4.1%。

數據公布後，2年期美國公債殖利率一度上升8個基點，終場上漲2.9個基點至4.367%。5年期上升3.1個基點至4.546%，10年期上升1.4個基點至4.783%，30年期則下降0.4個基點至5.244%。2年與10年期殖利率差收窄1.5個基點至41.6個基點，2年與30年期利差收窄3.3個基點至87.7個基點。

這種曲線變化反映了政策訊息。就業轉強且招聘範圍擴大，使勞動市場不再是聯邦基金利率再次上調的眼前障礙，但尚不足以證明薪資與物價重新加速。平均時薪較7月上升0.3%，年增率卻放緩至3.1%，為2021年以來最低。10年期實質殖利率上升1.5個基點至2.43%，10年期損益兩平通膨率則幾乎持平於2.353%。投資人上調預期政策利率路徑，當日卻未要求更高的長期通膨補償。

交換市場顯示，9月升息25個基點的機率由就業報告公布前的約五成升至接近60%，並反映年底前累計升息35個基點。最終決定仍取決於通膨。聯準會理事Christopher Waller曾表示，若物價持續改善，便可支持再次按兵不動；在7月維持利率不變的決策中投下反對票的克里夫蘭聯準銀行總裁Beth Hammack則於週五表示，政策對經濟的抑制仍不充分，現在是採取行動的時候。

風險市場消化了利率調整，未出現廣泛去槓桿。標普500指數下跌0.38%，但納斯達克100指數上漲0.21%，半導體指數上漲3.38%，VIX收於14.53。美國投資級與高收益債利差變動不大，硬通貨新興市場債利差小幅收窄。這份韌性顯示，當日行情主要是重新定價聯準會風險，而非投資人全面逃離信用資產。

能源仍是解讀薪資放緩時最主要的反向力量。WTI收於$91.48，Brent收於$96.28，全週分別上漲9.69%與7.8%。就業報告顯示，即使面臨燃料衝擊，企業仍持續增聘員工；但原油價格居高不下，也繼續威脅物價改善，而這正是聯準會9月維持利率不變所需的條件。

## 招聘擴大但未重燃薪資升勢

8月就業報告不僅表面數字強勁，修正幅度與招聘廣度也同步改善。6月新增就業由2萬人上修至3.1萬人，7月則由減少2.3萬人修正為增加2.1萬人。兩個月合計上修5.5萬人，改寫了近期看似明顯疲弱的就業走勢，也使8月增幅遠高於此前12個月平均的3.1萬人。

民間就業在7月增加7.1萬人後，8月增加12.7萬人。政府就業則由減少5萬人轉為增加3.5萬人，其中地方政府教育部門增加4.2萬人。不過，這波反彈大致抵銷該部門7月的降幅，使地方教育就業較2025年1月幾乎沒有淨變化，因此部分改善反映公立學校暑期就業數據常見的時點波動。

餐飲服務場所增加5.9萬個職位，遠高於過去一年平均每月增加1.2萬人。營建業就業增加2.2萬人；製造業增加1.6萬人，其中機械及金屬製品業各增6,000人，使工廠就業較2025年12月增加5.8萬人。

民間產業的招聘分布也更廣。民間部門擴散指數由52.8升至55.6，製造業擴散指數由52.1升至61.1。這些指標衡量的是增加就業的產業占比，而非創造職位的速度，但仍顯示改善並非只集中於少數大型產業。

報告中仍有顯著弱點。資訊業就業減少2.3萬人，流失職位遍及運算基礎設施與資料處理、出版及廣播業；金融活動就業減少1.1萬人。醫療保健業僅增加1.3萬人，遠低於過去12個月平均的3.2萬人，儘管居家照護與醫院就業分別增加1.1萬人及8,000人。

這種分化符合當前經濟樣貌：營建、製造與實體基礎設施正在吸納勞工，若干資訊密集產業卻裁減人力。即使人工智慧相關投資持續支撐設備、電力與營建需求，資訊與金融活動兩個產業合計仍流失3.4萬個職位。這項結果在一定程度上支持一種看法，即投資熱潮正在改變就業結構，而非平均推升各產業就業。

家庭調查數據也有改善。家庭調查就業人數增加56.9萬人，勞動力擴大68.3萬人。勞動參與率由61.4%升至61.6%，為近一年來首次改善；就業人口比率則由58.9%升至59.1%。25至54歲勞工的參與率維持83.4%，顯示增幅集中於較年輕及較年長族群。

因此，失業率維持4.1%的同時，勞動力規模也在擴大，而非單靠參與率下滑來維持。因經濟因素從事非自願兼職的人數減少41.4萬至440萬。長期失業人數仍高達190萬，占全體失業人口27%；另有570萬名未計入勞動力的人士表示希望工作。

工時與薪資則提供較有保留的需求訊號。民間部門每週平均工時由34.3小時增至34.4小時，製造業工時增至40.5小時，工廠加班時數維持3.1小時。儘管時薪年增率放緩，就業人數增加及平均工時延長，仍有助於總體勞動所得與短期消費。

8月平均時薪上升0.3%至$37.75，生產及非主管職員工的平均時薪也上升0.3%至$32.53。整體薪資年增3.1%，意味直接勞動成本壓力不像非農就業表面數字那麼強，也有助於解釋為何短端殖利率上升時，長期通膨補償並未跟進。

對聯準會而言，這份報告改變了風險平衡，卻未替政策決定定案。即使通膨仍令人不安，疲弱的就業報告原本也可能使9月升息變得困難；實際數據排除了這項限制：招聘加速、先前的疲弱數據遭到上修、參與率改善，增加人力的產業也變多。不過，薪資年增率放緩，仍讓官員有空間判斷勞動市場雖穩健，卻尚未成為新的通膨來源。

Hammack提供了當日最明確的新政策訊號。她表示，最新數據及與轄區企業的對話都顯示，貨幣政策對經濟活動的抑制不夠。她提到，美國俄亥俄州東北部一家製造商表示許多投入價格出現兩位數漲幅，並要求聯準會升息。Hammack是7月主張升息25個基點而投下反對票的3名決策者之一，因此這次行動主張與她先前的投票立場直接相連。

她的立場進一步凸顯決策委員會內部的分歧。Waller表示，若8月通膨報告仍屬合理，他傾向維持利率不變；紐約聯準銀行總裁John Williams則強調通膨已有進展，能源價格上漲的外溢效應有限。聯準會主席Kevin Warsh指出，通膨必須明顯放緩，並認為勞動市場符合充分就業狀態。週五數據公布後，僅為保護成長而延後升息的就業理由已所剩無幾，是否採取行動如今必須由通膨決定。

美國總統Donald Trump採取相反立場，在強勁就業數據公布後要求降息，並威脅，若聯準會不從，將停止與美國對其有貿易逆差的國家進行貿易。白宮經濟顧問Kevin Hassett提出較傳統的政策論點，稱就業數字強化了維持利率不變的理由。兩人的發言都不會改變決策委員會在9月16日前將收到的通膨數據，但再度升高的公開施壓，為原已勢均力敵的決策增添政治變數。

## 前端重新定價，長端升勢受限

非農就業公布後，美國公債立即出現強烈反應，但接近收盤時行情轉為分化。2年期殖利率盤中最多上升8個基點，反映9月升息機率提高；最終僅上升2.9個基點，5年期則上升3.1個基點，顯示投資人重新把焦點放回尚未解決的通膨問題後，初步走勢已有部分回吐。

較長天期公債抵抗了前端賣壓。10年期殖利率僅上升1.4個基點，30年期更小幅下降，儘管兩者仍接近多年高點。因此，殖利率曲線趨平反映的是政策路徑調整，而非長端再度因財政疑慮而失守。30年期殖利率報5.244%，仍為政府借款、能源不確定性及資本競爭提供可觀補償，但非農就業並未顯著增加這些較長期風險。

實質殖利率與損益兩平通膨率的拆解也支持這項判斷。10年期名目殖利率的升幅，幾乎完全由實質殖利率上升1.5個基點至2.43%所解釋，損益兩平通膨率則下降0.1個基點。就業改善推高預期實質政策路徑及經濟韌性，卻未使市場的長期通膨指標再度上升。

在經歷波動劇烈的一週後，這項區別尤其重要。10年期殖利率曾觸及3年高點，30年期則仍接近全球金融危機前最後見到的水準。全週10年期上升6.3個基點，30年期上升3.7個基點。就業數據延續了殖利率壓力，卻未重演先前由能源帶動的曲線陡峭化，也未迫使最長天期再度提供額外讓利。

跨資產交易同樣保持有序。相對利率前景轉為有利美元，美元指數週五上漲0.16%，但全週仍下跌0.54%。黃金期貨下跌1.38%至$4,429.80；就業數據公布後，隨殖利率與美元上升，現貨黃金一度下跌2.4%。比特幣盤中跌破$80,000。跌勢集中於對實質殖利率和政策預期敏感的資產，並未伴隨風險資產全面撤退。

股票市場也呈現同樣的區別。標普500指數下跌0.38%，科技股卻保持穩健，半導體股更大幅上漲；標普500指數全週仍小幅收高。信用風險溢酬維持低檔，銀行放款持續增加，投資級債發行也未因先前政府公債殖利率上升而中斷。基準利率上升提高了資金成本，但尚未妨礙信用較強的借款人取得資金。

不過，整體穩定掩蓋了美國公債本身的需求分化。穩定幣發行商一度被視為短期政府融資的潛在大型新需求來源，但隨加密貨幣交易轉弱，今年上半年穩定幣供給反而萎縮。Tether的USDT供給減少近$30億至約$1,840億，Circle的USDC也減少相近金額至約$720億。

Tether申報持有約$1,340億美國公債及以政府債券擔保的附買回協議資產，Circle則持有約$630億。美國財政部長Scott Bessent曾預測，穩定幣市場到本世紀末可擴大10倍至$3兆，進而對規模約$7兆的國庫券市場創造需求。近期萎縮不會逆轉既有持倉，卻削弱了穩定幣短期內能吸收大批新增發行的論點。

支付與跨境交易是另一條潛在成長管道。7月以穩定幣進行的卡片支付超過$10億，另有估算顯示穩定幣年支付量接近$3,900億。然而，既有代幣被反覆使用，並不必然要求發行商增發穩定幣或購買更多美國公債作為擔保品。對政府融資而言，交易量成長只有在帶動穩定幣流通餘額增加時才具實質意義。

這波短期需求暫停之際，美國財政部正更加依賴國庫券，並擴大回購較長天期證券。穩定幣發行商仍是重要持有人，但其規模擴張與加密貨幣市場活動緊密相連，並不直接取決於政府融資需求。相較於一個仍在發展中的投資人基礎所帶來的預期成長，即將進行的標售與回購操作，才是更直接的民間需求考驗。

## 信用市場仍暢通，但受償順位與燃料成本造成分化

美國整體信用市場對非農就業幾乎沒有反應。投資級與高收益債利差收盤變動不大，主要上市基金跌幅均低於0.1%；硬通貨新興市場債利差則小幅收窄。不過，平靜的指數表現背後，融資條件、擔保品保障及重整風險的差異異常顯著。

科技公司債顯示，供給可以創造相對價值，卻不代表信用基本面普遍惡化。DoubleLine的Robert Cohen表示，大型高評等雲端運算公司的債券正變得更具吸引力，因人工智慧融資一再湧現，已使科技業利差擴大。投資級科技債利差較整體高評等市場寬近10個基點，數家大型發行人的信用違約交換價格也持續上升。

Alphabet於8月發行的10年期債券，交易利差約為可比美國公債之上81個基點。該公司2月發行的10年期債券，利差較發行時擴大約15個基點至約76個基點。整體高評等債券指數利差約80個基點，但Alphabet獲標普評為AA+，信用素質明顯優於指數平均；Amazon的評等則為AA。

關鍵在於技術性供給消化不良，而非基本面受損。大型科技公司獲利與資產負債表強健，但反覆舉債可能壓倒短期需求，排擠評等較低的企業或資料中心專案。即使最大型發行人的融資能力仍相當充足，大型雲端運算公司利差擴大，也可能迫使風險較高的借款人提供更多補償。

日本零售債市場則顯示，信用融資管道正因應政府公債殖利率上升而調整。SoftBank Group將一筆¥1兆、7年期債券的票息定為4.9%，位於指示區間頂端，並超過今年日圓零售公司債平均票息2.3%的兩倍。這筆交易使日本零售債截至9月4日的銷售額增至¥2.88兆，已超越歷年任何一個完整年度。

日本10年期基準公債殖利率高於3%，使固定收益產品相較存款與股票更能吸引家庭投資人。SoftBank票息還包含可觀的信用溢酬：日本國內信評機構將該公司列為投資級，主要國際信評機構卻給予非投資級評等。這筆交易使SoftBank的資金來源更多元，也顯示只要補償充分，家庭需求足以吸收規模異常龐大的發行。

Air Baltic則位於融資壓力最嚴重的一端。這家獲政府支持的航空公司要求債券持有人於9月11日表決，是否同意由Polus Capital Management及Klirmark Capital主導、最高€2.57億的過渡融資。Polus將認購至少一半的新發超級優先債券；若其他債權人不參與，兩檔基金將包銷其餘部分。

這筆過渡融資的年利率為25%。Polus與Klirmark另將取得價值約€3,000萬、以額外超級優先債券支付的費用。參與的債券持有人可將部分既有2029年到期債券交換為受償順位更高的債務；未參與者的順位則將落後於新資金提供者及換入升級順位債券的持有人。

首期發行將提供€1.8億。第2期款項部分取決於Air Baltic能否與利害關係人達成重整協議，新發超級優先債務則於2027年2月26日到期。持有航空公司88%股權及約13%既有債券的拉脫維亞，在國會授權認購後，最多可提供€3,000萬新資金。這些條款顯示，融資只是通往更廣泛重整的臨時周轉空間，並未解決資本結構問題。

燃料壓力有助於解釋如此高昂的融資價格。中東戰事推升成本後，Air Baltic已向拉脫維亞借款€3,000萬。在美國高收益債市場，隨航空燃油價格上漲、投資人重新評估小型航空公司將成本轉嫁給旅客的能力，航空業利差已接近400個基點，超過1月水準的兩倍。

燃料約占航空公司支出20%。United Airlines在最近一輪局勢升級前借款，其5年期債券於2月以5.375%定價；評等同樣接近BB的Alaska Air則於5月為5年期債務支付6.5%。大型國際航空公司可透過高端旅運需求及較高票價抵銷部分成本增幅；小型國內航空公司的旅客對價格較敏感，保護利潤率的空間也較小。

JetBlue票息9.875%、2031年到期、以忠誠度計畫擔保的債券，價格在每$1面額約84美分，低於2月的約104美分。公司討論獲利及資產負債表後，債券價格一度回升，但燃料疑慮再起，抹去部分漲幅。這個例子說明，即使整體高收益債指數保持穩定，單一產業的營運衝擊仍可能大幅改變再融資條件。

印尼國營企業則呈現逾期付款與國內融資能力之間的另一種連結。建築商PT Adhi Karya未能支付前一週到期、約608億印尼盾、即$340萬的債券利息。該公司正進行重整，並安排9月11日召開債券持有人會議，以處理由這筆逾期付款衍生的債務責任。

在前總統Joko Widodo推動基礎建設期間，4家主要國營建築商的債務增加12倍至約124兆印尼盾，去年底仍接近118兆印尼盾。2025年成立的主權財富基金Danantara管理超過800家國營企業，並尋求將數量縮減至約200家。官員估計其控制的資產約值$9,000億。

相較於該基金彼此競爭的各項義務，建築商負債規模相當龐大。Danantara今年預計向政府繳交120兆印尼盾，主要來自國營企業股利，金額接近4家建築商的合計債務。該基金去年曾向Garuda Indonesia注資23.7兆印尼盾，顯示救助確有可能，但每次救援都會壓縮可供新投資的資本，或增加基金本身的借款需求。

壓力已蔓延至建築業以外。PT Pos Indonesia於7月未支付241億印尼盾的伊斯蘭債券票息後，確認2023至2025年涉及9兆印尼盾的會計調整；公司其後已支付票息及額外補償。國營銀行是公共企業的主要放款人，隨重整推進，可能面臨到期日展延、本金減記或長期持有受壓曝險。

民間借款人也在爭取同一銀行資金池。PT Jababeka於6月利用Bank Mandiri提供的長期融資，償還$1.859億美元債券；PT Modernland Realty則正為明年到期、約$2.745億的美元債務尋求5年內第3次重整。真正的疑慮與其說是全國性的國營企業危機，不如說是Danantara、陷入困境的公共企業與民間借款人，都在競爭由政府主導的國內信用資源。

塞內加爾進一步接近強制性主權債務重整。標普全球評級將該國評等由CCC+降至CC，展望為負向，並表示其外幣商業債務極可能出現困境債務交換或違約。政府在與IMF就一項$22億計畫達成工作人員層級協議後，已宣布依20國集團共同框架進行債務處理，但IMF計畫仍待董事會批准。

塞內加爾表示，非洲金融共同體法郎債務將排除在處理範圍之外，並將繼續償付所有債務，包括9月13日應支付的2048年到期歐元債券款項。但標普仍質疑，在足以恢復債務可持續性的方案中，規模龐大的本幣債務能否置身事外。處理範圍尚未確定，使外國債權人與區域金融機構都暴露於最終方案的風險。

Citigroup認為，西非開發銀行、Afreximbank、Africa Finance Corp.及Ecobank對不利的重整情境尤其敏感。BOAD對塞內加爾的曝險約占放款組合17%，Afreximbank低於4%，Ecobank約6%，AFC約8%；以上數據不含結構型主權流動性交易。IMF批准延後、對多邊機構逾期付款、優先債權人待遇受到挑戰，或將非洲金融共同體法郎債務納入處理範圍，都會提高這些放款人的風險，並可能限制當地企業取得信貸。

結構型信用市場也再次警示，不能把平靜的指數解讀為各處風險紀律一致。Pimco總裁Christian Stracke表示，部分擔保基金債務憑證與重大風險移轉工具，對其內含槓桿提供的補償不足。CFO把基金股權轉換為具信評的債務，買方通常包括保險公司；風險移轉工具則讓銀行把貸款曝險移交第三方。

基金融資市場規模超過$1兆，這些結構也正在亞洲擴張，包括Seviora與Churchill Asset Management完成的一筆$4億CFO。Pimco不認為這類工具構成系統性威脅，並將當前槓桿與全球金融危機前的多層借貸區別開來。其疑慮較為具體：即使風險仍集中於複雜擔保品與受償順位結構，高評等與槓桿仍可能促使投資人接受不足的風險溢酬。

## 日本利差交易平倉引領全球利率路徑分化

在美國交易時段前後，日本市場出現全球幅度最大的重新定價。日圓全週升值約2.4%，為7月以來最佳表現，匯價接近每美元156日圓。投資人平倉以日圓融資的利差交易，並提高對日本央行加快緊縮的預期。

日本2年期殖利率全週上升約14個基點。交換市場已反映9月18日會議升息25個基點，並反映到明年7月前接近再升息3次、每次25個基點；相較2024年以來平均每年約升息兩次，步調明顯加快。投資人回補日圓空頭部位之際，週四日圓兌美元買權成交量超過賣權的2.5倍。

現有部位仍留下進一步調整空間。截至8月25日當週，槓桿基金淨放空日圓81,619口，資產管理機構則淨放空18,284口。日本出口商也增加美元賣盤。因此，這波匯率走勢是政策重新定價、空頭回補與企業資金流共同作用的結果，而非單一交易所致。

野村策略師Yujiro Goto表示，若日圓再度走弱並逼近160，日本央行一路到12月連續3次各升息25個基點將是極端情境。他的基準預測較為溫和，認為每季至少升息一次，9月行動看來合理。關鍵限制在於日圓已明顯升值：若要維持漲勢，日本央行必須提供足夠的緊縮行動及政策指引，證實目前交換市場已反映的預期。

日圓走強也衝擊利差交易所使用的高收益貨幣。在平倉最激烈的階段，巴西里拉、南非蘭特及墨西哥披索兌日圓均下跌逾1%。美國就業報告公布後，這些貨幣兌美元回升；一項新興市場貨幣指數則連續第10週上漲，創2007年以來最長連漲紀錄。

本幣新興市場債今年報酬超過3%，美國公債及歐洲政府債則下跌約0.6%。部分開發中經濟體起始利率具限制性、通膨受控且財政狀況較強，使其較能抵禦主要主權債市場的賣壓。不過韌性並不一致：塞內加爾仍陷於困境，擁有較多政策空間或信評改善的國家則持續吸引資金。

哈薩克利用這項政策空間，連續第3次降息，將基準利率下調50個基點至16.25%。多數經濟學家原先預期降幅較小或維持不變。8月通膨年增率放緩至9.8%，為一年多來最低，堅戈在2026年兌美元也已升值近11%。

不過，哈薩克國家銀行表示，進一步寬鬆的空間已縮小。通膨仍接近其中期目標5%的兩倍，央行並將2027年通膨預測由5.5%-7.5%上調至6.5%-8.5%，今年底預測區間則維持9%-11%。財政移轉、受管制費率及堅戈是否逆轉走勢，將決定利率能否在年底前降至16%-16.25%區間以下。

紐西蘭央行也進一步說明緊縮路徑的時點。助理總裁Karen Silk表示，若前景依預期發展，可能再次升息，但12月採取行動的機率高於10月。市場認為10月升息至3%的機率為31%，並已完全反映12月前升至該水準。

在6人組成的貨幣政策委員會中，Silk是強調通膨上行風險的4名委員之一。她提到中東衝突持續時間、燃料與運費成本的傳導、經濟成長復甦後企業提高價格的能力，以及保險、電力與土地稅等持續性的國內成本。她並未反對最近一次政策決定，強調紐西蘭央行仍保有彈性，未承諾預設的行動次序。

捷克通膨結果較為均衡。8月消費者物價年增1.9%，符合市場預測中位數與央行預估。服務通膨由4.7%放緩至4.5%，薪資數據也轉弱，支持央行在9月17日會議維持利率不變。然而，能源成本、食品價格及擴大的財政赤字，仍可能使通膨在2027年初升破3%。

英國公債大幅下跌後開始吸引買盤。Aviva Investors在10年期殖利率接近5.15%時加碼，該水準僅略低於本週創下的19年高點。這家管理£2,530億資產的機構認為，價格已大致反映財政風險，殖利率上升本身也會限制政府的支出選擇。

市場訊號並非全然正面。據估計，殖利率上升已使政府的財政緩衝減少約£120億，令10月28日預算案更為關鍵。不過，資產交換利差大致持平，顯示最近走勢較多反映通膨及政策預期，而非市場對供給信心突然惡化。這項區別使長天期英國公債得以吸引買盤，即使英國財政對利率的敏感度仍高。

## 後續市場意義

美國接下來的通膨數據已成為9月16日聯準會決策的主導因素。8月生產者物價將於9月10日美東時間上午8:30公布。整體PPI預計在7月持平後上升0.3%，核心PPI則預計由0.2%加速至0.3%。排除食品、能源及貿易的指標月增率預計由0.4%放緩至0.3%，年增率則由4.7%降至4.4%。

初領失業救濟金人數將於同一時間公布，市場預期由20.6萬人降至約20.5萬人；續領失業救濟金人數則將公布截至8月29日當週數據，前值為177.9萬人。非農就業已減輕市場對招聘的憂慮，但申請數據將檢驗調查期過後裁員率是否仍處低檔。

CPI將於9月11日美東時間上午8:30公布。整體物價預計較7月上升0.4%，年增率維持3.4%；核心通膨預計月增0.2%、年增2.4%，低於前值2.5%。較溫和的核心數據將支持Waller的觀點，即使就業轉強，聯準會仍可等待；若物價漲勢範圍擴大或持續加速，則會強化Hammack主張立即行動的理由。

能源將決定決策者能否有信心根據一次通膨數據推斷後續趨勢。Brent週五收於$96以上，美國固定收益市場收盤後，荷姆茲海峽周邊衝突仍在延續。美軍通報襲擊伊朗原油油輪後，伊朗於週末表示已攻擊3艘油輪及多艘與美國有關的船舶。這些稍晚發生的事件並非週五美國公債走勢的原因，卻提高了燃料成本在評估通膨數據及聯準會預測時持續居高不下的風險。

美國公債供給是另一項考驗。3年期公債定於9月8日標售，10年期及30年期分別於9月9日與10日標售。較短天期標售的需求將反映重新定價後的聯準會利率路徑；10年期及30年期標售則將檢驗接近4.8%與5.25%的殖利率，是否足以補償財政供給、公司債發行及能源不確定性。

美國財政部也預定於9月9日宣布下一次擴大長天期債券回購，並於翌日執行。財政部已承諾至少把先前$20億的上限提高一倍，同時保留更大增幅的可能性。若購買額超過$40億，可能為長端提供支撐，但回購只是重新分配市場上的存續期間與流動性，並不會消除政府融資需求。

市場普遍預期歐洲央行將於9月10日把存款利率上調25個基點至2.5%。經濟學家多數認為這將是最後一次升息，市場反映的利率路徑直到2027年中卻明顯更高，因此對12月的政策指引將比預期中的升息決定更重要。歐元區8月通膨升至3.3%，核心通膨則放緩；後續前景取決於能源衝擊是否擴散至薪資及更廣泛的服務價格。

同一天還有另一批歐洲及全球數據，包括挪威通膨與美國住宅數據。英國方面，英格蘭銀行官員赴國會作證及隨後公布的成長數據，將顯示接近數十年高點的殖利率，能否在10月預算案前充分抑制經濟活動，以抵銷能源通膨。

即使市場已反映升息25個基點，日本央行9月18日會議仍是亞洲最重要的政策事件。日圓上漲與利差交易平倉，已提高央行例行升息卻只提供有限指引的代價。若央行按一般幅度升息，同時對其後加快行動保持開放，便能證實部分最新部位配置；若態度猶豫，則可能逆轉部分空頭回補，並重新引發市場對日圓朝每美元160走弱的擔憂。

信用市場面臨更近的合約期限。Air Baltic債券持有人將於9月11日表決€2.57億超級優先過渡融資、25%票息及未參與者順位下降的安排。Adhi Karya在未支付608億印尼盾利息後，也安排同日召開債券持有人會議。這些表決與協商將決定受償順位及過渡期流動性，而非兩家企業的最終價值。

塞內加爾9月13日應支付的2048年到期歐元債券款項，是下一項主權信用考驗。政府表示，在IMF計畫及共同框架債務處理推進期間，仍將繼續償債。按時付款可維持其短期立場，卻無法解決標普如今認為極可能出現的本金、利息或到期條件調整。

非農就業報告為聯準會提供了緊縮空間，卻沒有迫使其升息。通膨必須決定9月投票結果；標售必須顯示民間需求能否吸收高檔的美國公債與公司債供給；信用事件期限則將決定哪些借款人能把仍然暢通的市場轉化為持久融資，而非僅獲得暫時喘息。

overall_summary.headline: 就業強勁推升短天期美債殖利率，長端通膨定價保持穩定
overall_summary.session_narrative:
美國8月非農就業增加16.2萬人，高於所有預估；修正後6月與7月合計增加5.5萬人，並抹去原先公布的7月就業萎縮。失業率維持4.1%。2年期美國公債殖利率一度上升8個基點，終場上漲2.9個基點至4.367%；10年期上升1.4個基點至4.783%，30年期則下降0.4個基點至5.244%。2年與10年期殖利率差收窄1.5個基點至41.6個基點。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

A broad rebound in US hiring pushed Treasury yields higher on Sept. 4 and restored a Federal Reserve rate increase to the center of the September debate, but the selloff remained concentrated in shorter maturities. Nonfarm payrolls rose 162,000 in August, topping every estimate in Bloomberg’s survey, while revisions erased July’s previously reported contraction and added 55,000 jobs across June and July. The unemployment rate held at 4.1%.

The 2-year Treasury yield climbed as much as 8 basis points after the release before ending 2.9 basis points higher at 4.367%. The 5-year rose 3.1 basis points to 4.546%, the 10-year added 1.4 basis points to 4.783%, and the 30-year slipped 0.4 basis point to 5.244%. The 2s10s curve flattened 1.5 basis points to 41.6 basis points, while 2s30s narrowed 3.3 basis points to 87.7.

That shape captured the policy message. Stronger employment and wider hiring breadth removed the labor market as an immediate obstacle to another increase in the federal funds rate. They did not, however, establish a renewed wage-price acceleration. Average hourly earnings rose 0.3% from July but slowed to 3.1% from a year earlier, the weakest annual increase since 2021. The 10-year real yield rose 1.5 basis points to 2.43%, while the 10-year breakeven was almost unchanged at 2.353%. Investors marked up the prospective policy path without demanding additional long-run inflation compensation on the day.

Swaps put the probability of a quarter-point September increase near 60%, from roughly even odds before payrolls, and priced 35 basis points of tightening through year-end. The decision still turns on inflation. Governor Christopher Waller has said continued progress in prices would support another hold, while Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack, a dissenter from July’s decision to leave rates unchanged, said Friday that policy was not restraining the economy sufficiently and that it was time to act.

Risk markets absorbed the rate adjustment without broad deleveraging. The S&P 500 declined 0.38%, but the Nasdaq 100 rose 0.21% and the semiconductor index gained 3.38%. The VIX finished at 14.53. US investment-grade and high-yield spreads were little changed, while hard-currency emerging-market spreads tightened modestly. That resilience left the session as a repricing of Fed risk rather than a general flight from credit.

Energy remained the principal counterforce to any benign reading of slower wages. WTI ended at $91.48 and Brent at $96.28, leaving them 9.69% and 7.8% higher over the week. The employment report showed that firms were still adding workers through the fuel shock, while elevated crude continued to threaten the inflation improvement on which a September hold would depend.

## Hiring Broadens Without Rekindling Wage Acceleration

The August employment report was stronger not only in its headline but also in its revisions and breadth. June payroll growth was revised to 31,000 from 20,000, while July was revised to a gain of 21,000 from a loss of 23,000. The combined 55,000 upward revision replaced a recent sequence that had appeared materially weaker and lifted the latest gain well above the preceding 12-month average of 31,000.

Private payrolls rose 127,000 after 71,000 in July. Government employment added 35,000 after falling 50,000, with local-government education gaining 42,000. That rebound largely reversed the sector’s July decline, however, and left little net change in local education employment since January 2025. Part of the improvement therefore reflected the timing volatility that often affects public-school payrolls during the summer.

Food services and drinking places added 59,000 jobs, compared with an average monthly gain of 12,000 over the previous year. Construction increased employment by 22,000. Manufacturing added 16,000, including gains of 6,000 each in machinery and fabricated metals, taking factory employment 58,000 higher since December 2025.

Hiring was more widely distributed within private industry. The private-sector diffusion index rose to 55.6 from 52.8, while its manufacturing counterpart increased to 61.1 from 52.1. Those measures describe the share of industries increasing employment, not the pace of job creation, but they showed that the improvement extended beyond a few large categories.

The report still contained meaningful areas of weakness. Information employment fell 23,000, including losses in computing infrastructure and data processing, publishing, and broadcasting. Financial activities shed 11,000. Health care added only 13,000, well below its 12-month average of 32,000, even with an 11,000 increase in home health and an 8,000 gain at hospitals.

That split was consistent with an economy in which construction, manufacturing and physical infrastructure were absorbing workers while several information-intensive sectors reduced headcount. Information and financial activities lost a combined 34,000 jobs, even as investment associated with artificial intelligence continued to support equipment, power and construction demand. The result offered some support for the view that the investment boom is changing the composition of employment rather than uniformly lifting it.

Household data also improved. Employment in the household survey increased 569,000 and the labor force expanded by 683,000. The participation rate rose to 61.6% from 61.4%, its first improvement in almost a year, while the employment-to-population ratio increased to 59.1% from 58.9%. Participation among workers aged 25 to 54 was unchanged at 83.4%, leaving the increase concentrated among younger and older workers.

The unchanged 4.1% unemployment rate therefore coexisted with a larger workforce rather than being maintained solely through declining participation. The number of people working part time for economic reasons fell by 414,000 to 4.4 million. Long-term unemployment remained elevated at 1.9 million, accounting for 27% of all unemployed workers, and 5.7 million people outside the labor force said they wanted work.

Hours and earnings provided a qualified demand signal. The private-sector workweek increased to 34.4 hours from 34.3, while manufacturing hours rose to 40.5 and factory overtime held at 3.1 hours. More workers and a longer average week support aggregate labor income and near-term consumption, even though annual hourly-pay growth slowed.

Average hourly earnings reached $37.75 after increasing 0.3% during August. Production and nonsupervisory earnings also rose 0.3%, to $32.53. The 3.1% annual increase in overall wages suggested less direct labor-cost pressure than the payroll headline alone, helping explain why longer-term inflation compensation did not rise with short yields.

For the Fed, the release changed the balance of risks without settling the decision. A weak employment report could have made a September increase difficult even if inflation remained uncomfortable. The actual report removed that constraint: hiring accelerated, earlier weakness was revised away, participation improved and more industries added workers. The slower annual earnings rate nevertheless left room for officials to conclude that labor conditions are firm without becoming a new source of inflation.

Hammack supplied the session’s clearest new policy signal. The Cleveland Fed president said both incoming data and conversations in her district indicated that monetary policy was not weighing sufficiently on activity. She cited a Northeast Ohio manufacturer reporting double-digit increases in many input prices and asking the Fed to raise rates. Hammack had been one of three policymakers who dissented in July in favor of a quarter-point increase, giving her call for action a direct voting-history context.

Her position sharpened the contrast inside the committee. Waller has said he is inclined to hold if the August inflation reports remain reasonable, while New York Fed President John Williams has pointed to progress in inflation and limited spillover from higher energy prices. Chair Kevin Warsh has emphasized that inflation must be slowing meaningfully and described the labor market as consistent with full employment. After Friday’s release, employment offers little reason to delay solely for growth protection; inflation must now decide whether the committee acts.

President Donald Trump moved in the opposite direction, demanding lower rates after the strong jobs figures and threatening to stop trade with countries with which the US runs deficits if the Fed did not comply. White House economic adviser Kevin Hassett offered a more conventional policy argument, saying the employment numbers strengthened the case for holding rates steady. Neither intervention altered the inflation data the committee will receive before Sept. 16, but the renewed public pressure adds a political complication to an already close decision.

## The Front End Reprices While the Long End Finds a Ceiling

The Treasury reaction was forceful immediately after payrolls but became more selective into the close. The 2-year yield’s intraday increase of as much as 8 basis points reflected the rise in September hike probabilities. Its final 2.9-basis-point increase, alongside a 3.1-basis-point rise at 5 years, showed that some of the initial move was reversed as investors returned to the unresolved inflation question.

Longer maturities resisted the front-end selloff. The 10-year yield rose only 1.4 basis points and the 30-year edged lower, even though both remained close to multiyear highs. The curve flattening was therefore a policy-path move rather than a renewed long-end fiscal break. At 5.244%, the 30-year yield still carried considerable compensation for government borrowing, energy uncertainty and competition for capital, but payrolls did not add materially to those longer-horizon risks.

The real-yield and breakeven decomposition reinforced that reading. The nominal 10-year increase was matched by a 1.5-basis-point rise in the real yield to 2.43%, while the breakeven eased 0.1 basis point. Better hiring lifted the expected real policy path and growth resilience without creating another daily increase in the market’s long-term inflation measure.

That distinction matters after a volatile week in which the 10-year yield had reached a three-year high and the 30-year remained near levels last seen before the global financial crisis. Over the week, the 10-year rose 6.3 basis points and the 30-year gained 3.7. Payrolls extended the pressure but did not reproduce the earlier energy-driven steepening or force another concession at the longest maturity.

Cross-asset trading also remained orderly. The Dollar Index gained 0.16% on Friday as the relative-rate outlook moved in the dollar’s favor, though it still fell 0.54% over the week. Gold futures declined 1.38% to $4,429.80, and spot bullion had fallen as much as 2.4% after the employment release as yields and the dollar rose. Bitcoin dropped below $80,000 intraday. Those moves were concentrated in assets sensitive to real yields and policy expectations rather than accompanied by a wholesale retreat from risk.

Equities showed the same discrimination. The S&P 500 lost 0.38%, while technology shares held up and semiconductors rallied sharply. The S&P still finished the week marginally higher. Credit premiums remained subdued, bank lending was still expanding, and investment-grade issuance had continued through the preceding rise in government yields. Higher benchmark rates raised the cost of money, but they had not yet impaired its availability to stronger borrowers.

The stability masks uneven demand for Treasury securities themselves. Stablecoin issuers, once presented as a potentially large new source of short-term government financing, contracted during the first half of the year as cryptocurrency trading weakened. The supply of Tether’s USDT fell by nearly $3 billion to about $184 billion, while Circle’s USDC declined by a similar amount to roughly $72 billion.

Tether reported about $134 billion of Treasuries and reverse-repurchase agreements backed by government debt, and Circle about $63 billion. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent had projected that the stablecoin market could expand tenfold to $3 trillion by the end of the decade, creating demand for a bill market of roughly $7 trillion. The recent contraction does not reverse those holdings, but it weakens the near-term case that stablecoins will absorb a meaningful share of additional issuance.

Payments and cross-border transactions offer another potential growth channel: stablecoin-based card payments exceeded $1 billion in July, while one estimate put annual stablecoin payment volume near $390 billion. Yet repeated use of an existing token does not necessarily require issuers to create additional coins or buy more Treasury collateral. For government funding, transaction growth matters only to the extent that it expands outstanding stablecoin balances.

The short-term demand pause arrives as Treasury is relying more heavily on bills and increasing buybacks of longer-dated securities. Stablecoin issuers remain substantial holders, but their expansion is tied closely to crypto-market activity rather than directly to the government’s financing requirement. That makes the coming auctions and buyback operation a more immediate test of private demand than projected growth from a developing investor base.

## Credit Stays Open, but Priority and Fuel Costs Divide Borrowers

Broad US credit barely reacted to payrolls. Investment-grade and high-yield spreads ended little changed, and their principal listed funds posted declines of less than 0.1%. Hard-currency emerging-market spreads tightened modestly. The calm index result coexisted with unusually wide differences in funding terms, collateral protection and restructuring risk.

Technology bonds illustrated how supply can create relative value without implying broad credit deterioration. DoubleLine’s Robert Cohen said the debt of highly rated hyperscalers was becoming more attractive after repeated artificial-intelligence financing widened sector spreads. Investment-grade technology spreads were nearly 10 basis points wider than the overall high-grade market, and credit-default-swap prices on several large issuers had been rising.

Alphabet’s 10-year bonds issued in August traded around 81 basis points over comparable Treasuries. Its 10-year notes sold in February had widened about 15 basis points from issuance to roughly 76 basis points. The broad high-grade index spread was about 80 basis points even though Alphabet, rated AA+ by S&P, carried materially stronger credit quality than the index average. Amazon was rated AA.

The distinction was between technical indigestion and fundamental impairment. Large technology companies have strong earnings and balance sheets, but their repeated borrowing can overwhelm near-term demand and crowd out lower-rated companies or data-center projects. Wider hyperscaler spreads may force riskier borrowers to offer more compensation even when the largest issuers retain ample capacity.

Japan’s retail market supplied another example of credit access adapting to higher government yields. SoftBank Group priced a ¥1 trillion seven-year bond at 4.9%, the top of its indicated range and more than twice the 2.3% average coupon on yen retail corporate issuance this year. The transaction helped take Japanese retail bond sales to ¥2.88 trillion through Sept. 4, already above every previous full-year total.

Yields above 3% on benchmark 10-year Japanese government bonds have made fixed income more competitive with deposits and equities for households. SoftBank’s coupon added a large credit premium: domestic rating agencies classify the company as investment grade, while major global agencies rate it speculative grade. The deal diversified SoftBank’s funding base and showed that household demand could absorb an unusually large transaction when compensation was sufficient.

Air Baltic occupied the stressed end of the financing spectrum. The state-backed airline asked holders to vote Sept. 11 on up to €257 million of interim financing led by Polus Capital Management and Klirmark Capital. Polus would subscribe to at least half of the new super-senior notes, and the two funds would backstop the remainder if other creditors declined to participate.

The bridge carries a 25% annual interest rate. Polus and Klirmark would also receive fees worth about €30 million in additional super-senior notes. Participating holders could exchange part of their existing 2029 bonds into higher-ranking debt, while nonparticipants would fall behind the new-money providers and holders of the uptiered instruments.

The initial issue would provide €180 million. A second installment depends in part on Air Baltic reaching a restructuring agreement with stakeholders, and the new super-senior debt matures on Feb. 26, 2027. Latvia, which owns 88% of the airline and about 13% of its existing bonds, can provide as much as €30 million of new money after parliament authorized the purchase. The terms make the financing a temporary runway to a broader restructuring rather than a resolution of the capital structure.

Fuel pressure helps explain the price. Air Baltic had already borrowed €30 million from Latvia after Middle East fighting raised costs. Across the US high-yield market, airline spreads were close to 400 basis points, more than double their January level, as jet-fuel prices climbed and investors reassessed smaller carriers’ capacity to pass costs through to customers.

Fuel represents roughly 20% of airline expenses. United Airlines, which borrowed before the latest escalation, priced a five-year tranche at 5.375% in February. Alaska Air, with a similar BB rating, paid 6.5% for five-year debt in May. Large international carriers have offset some of the increase with premium demand and higher ticket prices, while smaller domestic airlines serve more price-sensitive passengers and have less room to protect margins.

JetBlue’s 9.875% loyalty-program-backed bonds due in 2031 traded near 84 cents on the dollar, down from about 104 in February. The notes had briefly recovered after the company discussed its earnings and balance sheet, but renewed fuel concerns erased part of that improvement. The example shows how a broad high-yield index can remain stable even when one sector’s operating shock sharply changes refinancing economics.

Indonesia’s state enterprises exposed a different connection between missed payments and domestic funding capacity. Builder PT Adhi Karya failed to pay about 60.8 billion rupiah, or $3.4 million, of bond interest due in the preceding week. It was undergoing restructuring and arranging a Sept. 11 bondholder meeting intended to address liability arising from the missed payment.

Debt at four major state builders had increased twelvefold to about 124 trillion rupiah during former President Joko Widodo’s infrastructure drive and stood near 118 trillion rupiah at the end of last year. Danantara, the sovereign wealth fund created in 2025, manages more than 800 state enterprises and is seeking to reduce that number to about 200. Officials value its controlled assets at roughly $900 billion.

The construction liabilities are large relative to the fund’s competing obligations. Danantara is expected to remit 120 trillion rupiah to the government this year, mainly from state-company dividends, an amount close to the four builders’ combined debt. It provided a 23.7 trillion rupiah capital injection to Garuda Indonesia last year, showing that support is possible, but each rescue reduces capital available for new investment or increases the fund’s own borrowing needs.

Stress has spread beyond builders. PT Pos Indonesia identified 9 trillion rupiah of accounting adjustments for 2023 through 2025 after missing a 24.1 billion rupiah sukuk coupon in July, though it subsequently paid the coupon and additional compensation. State-owned banks, the main lenders to public enterprises, may face maturity extensions, haircuts or prolonged stressed exposures as restructurings proceed.

Private borrowers are drawing on the same banking pool. PT Jababeka used long-term financing from Bank Mandiri to repay $185.9 million of dollar notes in June, while PT Modernland Realty was seeking a third restructuring in five years for about $274.5 million of dollar debt due next year. The concern is less an economy-wide state-enterprise crisis than competition among Danantara, troubled public companies and private borrowers for government-dominated domestic credit.

Senegal moved closer to a coercive sovereign restructuring. S&P Global Ratings lowered the country to CC from CCC+ with a negative outlook, saying a distressed exchange or default on foreign-currency commercial debt was extremely likely. The government had announced a debt treatment under the Group of 20 Common Framework after reaching a staff-level agreement on a $2.2 billion IMF program, which still requires board approval.

Senegal said CFA-franc obligations would be excluded and that it would continue servicing all debt, including a Sept. 13 payment on its 2048 eurobond. S&P nevertheless questioned whether the large stock of local-currency debt could remain outside a deal capable of restoring sustainability. The unresolved perimeter leaves both foreign creditors and regional institutions exposed to the eventual treatment.

Citigroup identified the West African Development Bank, Afreximbank, Africa Finance Corp. and Ecobank as particularly sensitive to adverse restructuring scenarios. BOAD’s Senegal exposure was about 17% of its loan book, compared with less than 4% at Afreximbank, approximately 6% at Ecobank and around 8% at AFC, excluding structured sovereign-liquidity transactions. Delayed IMF approval, missed payments to multilaterals, a challenge to preferred-creditor treatment or inclusion of CFA debt would increase the risk to those lenders and could restrict credit to local companies.

Structured credit provided one more warning against reading calm indices as uniform risk discipline. Pimco President Christian Stracke said some collateralized fund obligations and significant-risk-transfer instruments were not offering enough compensation for their embedded leverage. CFOs transform fund equity into rated debt, often for insurance-company buyers, while risk transfers allow banks to move loan exposure to third parties.

The fund-finance market exceeds $1 trillion, and the structures are expanding in Asia, including a $400 million CFO completed by Seviora and Churchill Asset Management. Pimco did not view the instruments as a systemic threat and distinguished current leverage from the layered borrowing preceding the global financial crisis. Its concern was narrower: high ratings and leverage can encourage investors to accept insufficient premiums even when risks remain concentrated in complex collateral and priority structures.

## Japan’s Carry Unwind Leads Diverging Global Rate Paths

Japan delivered the largest international repricing around the US session. The yen gained about 2.4% over the week, its best performance since July, and traded near 156 per dollar as investors unwound yen-funded carry positions and increased expectations for faster Bank of Japan tightening.

Two-year Japanese yields rose about 14 basis points over the week. Swaps priced a quarter-point increase at the Sept. 18 meeting and nearly three additional moves of the same size by July, a sharp acceleration from the average pace of roughly two increases a year since 2024. Yen call-option volume against the dollar was more than two and a half times put volume on Thursday as investors covered short-currency exposure.

Positioning left scope for further adjustment. Leveraged funds held a net short yen position of 81,619 contracts in the week ended Aug. 25, while asset managers were short 18,284. Japanese exporters also increased dollar sales. The currency move therefore combined policy repricing, short covering and corporate flows rather than reflecting one isolated transaction.

Nomura strategist Yujiro Goto described three consecutive quarter-point BOJ increases through December as an extreme scenario if renewed yen weakness pushed the currency toward 160. His baseline was less aggressive, calling for at least one increase per quarter, with a September move appearing reasonable. The key qualification is that the yen had already strengthened markedly: maintaining the rally requires the BOJ to deliver enough tightening and guidance to validate expectations now embedded in swaps.

A stronger yen also disrupted high-yielding currencies used in carry trades. The Brazilian real, South African rand and Mexican peso each fell more than 1% against the yen during the sharpest part of the unwind. They later recovered against the dollar after the US employment report, and an index of emerging-market currencies completed a 10th consecutive weekly gain, its longest winning streak since 2007.

Local-currency emerging-market bonds had returned more than 3% for the year, while US Treasuries and European government debt had lost about 0.6%. Restrictive starting rates, contained inflation and stronger fiscal positions in selected developing economies helped insulate them from the selloff in major sovereign markets. The resilience was uneven: Senegal remained distressed, while countries with greater policy room or improving ratings attracted capital.

Kazakhstan used that policy room to cut its benchmark by 50 basis points to 16.25%, its third consecutive reduction. Most economists had expected either a smaller move or no change. Annual inflation slowed to 9.8% in August, its lowest in more than a year, and the tenge had appreciated almost 11% against the dollar during 2026.

The National Bank of Kazakhstan nevertheless said the scope for further easing had narrowed. Inflation remained almost twice its 5% medium-term target, and the bank raised its 2027 inflation forecast to 6.5%-8.5% from 5.5%-7.5%. Its year-end range stayed at 9%-11%. Fiscal transfers, regulated tariffs and any reversal in the tenge will determine whether the rate can fall below the 16%-16.25% area by year-end.

New Zealand’s central bank also refined the timing of its tightening path. Assistant Governor Karen Silk said another increase was likely if the outlook evolved as expected, but December was more probable than October. Markets assigned a 31% chance to an October move to 3% and fully priced that level by December.

Silk was one of four members of the six-person Monetary Policy Committee who highlighted upside inflation risks. She cited the duration of the Middle East conflict, fuel and freight pass-through, firms’ ability to raise prices as growth recovers, and persistent domestic costs such as insurance, electricity and land taxes. She did not dissent from the latest decision, emphasizing that the RBNZ remained flexible rather than committed to a preset sequence.

Czech inflation supplied a more balanced result. Consumer prices rose 1.9% from a year earlier in August, matching both the median forecast and the central bank’s projection. Services inflation slowed to 4.5% from 4.7%, and softer wage data supported holding rates at the Sept. 17 meeting. Energy costs, food prices and a larger fiscal deficit still create a risk that inflation rises above 3% early in 2027.

UK gilts began attracting buyers after their sharp selloff. Aviva Investors added 10-year debt at yields near 5.15%, just below the week’s 19-year high. The £253 billion manager judged fiscal risk to be substantially reflected in prices and expected higher yields themselves to constrain the government’s spending choices.

The market signal was not uniformly benign. Rising yields were estimated to have removed about £12 billion from the government’s fiscal buffer, raising the stakes for the Oct. 28 budget. Asset-swap spreads remained broadly steady, however, suggesting the latest move reflected inflation and policy expectations more than an abrupt deterioration in supply confidence. That distinction helped long gilts recruit buyers even as Britain’s fiscal sensitivity remained high.

## Forward Market Significance

The US inflation sequence now dominates the Sept. 16 Fed decision. August producer prices are due Sept. 10 at 8:30 a.m. ET. Headline PPI is expected to rise 0.3% after no change in July, while core PPI is also expected at 0.3% after 0.2%. The measure excluding food, energy and trade is forecast to slow to 0.3% from 0.4%, and its annual rate to 4.4% from 4.7%.

Initial jobless claims arrive at the same time, with expectations close to 205,000 after 206,000, while continuing claims are due for the week ended Aug. 29 after a previous 1.779 million. Payrolls reduced concern about hiring, but claims will test whether low firing remains intact after the survey period.

CPI follows Sept. 11 at 8:30 a.m. ET. Headline prices are expected to rise 0.4% from July and remain 3.4% higher than a year earlier. Core inflation is expected at 0.2% monthly and 2.4% annually, down from 2.5%. A softer core reading would support Waller’s case that the Fed can wait despite stronger employment; broader or persistent acceleration would strengthen Hammack’s argument for immediate action.

Energy will determine how confidently policymakers can extrapolate from one inflation print. Brent ended Friday above $96 and the conflict around the Strait of Hormuz continued after the US fixed-income close. Over the weekend, Iran said it attacked three oil tankers and several US-linked vessels after the US military reported strikes against Iranian crude tankers. Those later events did not cause Friday’s Treasury move, but they raise the risk that fuel costs remain elevated when the inflation data and Fed forecasts are assessed.

Treasury supply presents a separate test. The 3-year note auction is scheduled for Sept. 8, followed by the 10-year on Sept. 9 and the 30-year on Sept. 10. Demand at the shorter sale will reflect the repriced Fed path, while the 10- and 30-year auctions will test whether yields near 4.8% and 5.25% provide sufficient compensation for fiscal supply, corporate issuance and energy uncertainty.

Treasury is also due to announce the next expanded long-maturity buyback on Sept. 9 for an operation the following day. The department has committed to at least doubling the previous $2 billion maximum, while leaving open a larger increase. A purchase above $4 billion could support the long end, but buybacks redistribute outstanding duration and liquidity rather than removing the government’s financing need.

The European Central Bank is widely expected to raise its deposit rate by 25 basis points to 2.5% on Sept. 10. Economists generally view that step as the final increase, while markets price a materially higher path through mid-2027. Guidance on December will therefore matter more than the anticipated decision. Euro-area inflation reached 3.3% in August, but core inflation slowed, leaving the outlook dependent on whether the energy shock spreads into wages and broader services prices.

The same day brings another round of European and global data, including Norwegian inflation and US housing figures. For the UK, parliamentary testimony from Bank of England officials and subsequent growth data will show whether yields near multidecade highs are tightening activity quickly enough to offset energy inflation before the October budget.

Japan’s Sept. 18 meeting remains the key Asian policy event even though a quarter-point increase is already priced. The yen rally and carry unwind have raised the cost of a routine decision with limited guidance. A standard increase accompanied by openness to faster subsequent moves would validate part of the latest positioning; hesitation could reverse some short covering and restore concern about renewed weakness toward 160 per dollar.

Credit faces nearer contractual deadlines. Air Baltic bondholders vote Sept. 11 on the €257 million super-senior bridge, its 25% coupon and the subordination of nonparticipants. Adhi Karya is arranging a bondholder meeting the same day after its missed 60.8 billion rupiah interest payment. Those votes and discussions will determine priority and interim liquidity, not the final value of either business.

Senegal’s Sept. 13 payment on its 2048 eurobond is the next sovereign test. The government has said it will keep servicing debt while the IMF program and Common Framework treatment proceed. Payment would preserve that near-term position without resolving the eventual reduction in principal, interest or maturity terms that S&P now considers extremely likely.

The payroll report gave the Fed room to tighten but did not force it to do so. Inflation must decide the September vote, auctions must show whether private demand can absorb elevated Treasury and corporate supply, and the credit deadlines will determine which borrowers can translate still-open markets into durable financing rather than temporary relief.

overall_summary.headline: Strong hiring lifts short Treasury yields as long-end inflation pricing holds
overall_summary.session_narrative:
US payrolls rose 162,000 in August, exceeding every estimate, while revisions added 55,000 jobs across June and July and erased July’s previously reported contraction. The unemployment rate held at 4.1%. The 2-year Treasury yield climbed as much as 8 basis points before closing 2.9 basis points higher at 4.367%; the 10-year added 1.4 basis points to 4.783%, and the 30-year slipped 0.4 basis point to 5.244%. The 2s10s curve flattened 1.5 basis points to 41.6 basis points.

Swaps raised the probability of a quarter-point September increase to near 60% from roughly even odds and priced 35 basis points of tightening through year-end. Annual wage growth nevertheless slowed to 3.1%, its weakest since 2021. The 10-year real yield rose 1.5 basis points to 2.43%, while the 10-year breakeven was almost unchanged at 2.353%, showing that investors raised the expected policy path without adding long-run inflation compensation. Hammack argued that policy was not restrictive enough, while Waller’s case for holding remained conditional on continued inflation progress.

Risk markets absorbed the adjustment without broad deleveraging. The S&P 500 fell 0.38%, but the Nasdaq 100 gained 0.21%, semiconductors rallied 3.38% and the VIX ended at 14.53. US investment-grade and high-yield spreads were little changed, while hard-currency emerging-market spreads tightened modestly. WTI at $91.48 and Brent at $96.28 remained the principal inflation risk after weekly gains of 9.69% and 7.8%.
overall_summary.summary: August payrolls beat every estimate and prior months were revised higher, moving a September Fed increase back toward the center of debate and flattening the Treasury curve, while slower annual wage growth and steady long-run inflation compensation kept the long end from joining the full selloff.
